claims.text: All three platform artifacts describe one trip: trip_id TRP-00114 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-07T18:40:00+08:00 matches the recorded start on the trip record. The rider has therefore carried limb (a) of the initial burden — the artifacts are of this trip and no identity objection is open.

The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record: under POL-RD-01 gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two disagree, so the actual distance is 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — a measured excess of 5.97 km. The trip record's 24.0 km may not be cited for the threshold test.

Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass on those figures: the excess is 33.17% of the 18.0 km optimal route, above the 20% test, and 5.97 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km test. The route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace and limb (b) of POL-RD-08 is satisfied.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 241 fixes at a 10 second sample interval across 100% coverage, no gaps at all and max_gap_sec of 0.0, and no consecutive-fix jump anywhere near the 500 m limb. No independent corroboration is therefore required for the deviation and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The only exculpatory route open to the driver is POL-RD-03, and it cannot run. I disclose that the artifact is impaired: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no payload — no LTA advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic_advisory naming an affected segment with an overlapping validity window; its absence is itself citable and it exonerates nothing. The driver's own statement concedes he knows of no advisory.

POL-RD-04 does not apply either. The two-message chat log shows the rider challenging the route — 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' at 18:58:40 — and the driver answering 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' at 18:59:20, which is an admission that the driver chose the corridor. There is no rider instruction, no named road requested by the rider, and waypoint_hint is null, so the rider-requested-detour clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

Nor was either endpoint amended: amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null and no pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at is recorded, so POL-RD-05 has no amended re-quote to re-price the trip against and cannot excuse any part of the 5.97 km excess.

The fare model on this trip is METERED, so the remedy is the arithmetic of POL-RD-02, not a discretionary payment. Recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30) x 1.6) + 0.80 + 2.50 = (25.70 x 1.6) + 3.30 = 41.12 + 3.30 = 44.42, where 1.6 is the surge_multiplier read from the fare breakdown (the rider does not contest the surge) and 2.50 is the ERP of the single gantry lying on the optimal route, the Kim Keat Link gantry.

Charged_total is 58.10, so the refund is 58.10 less 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 13.70. That is comfortably above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome for this rider-filed dispute is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70, leaving the rider not carrying the charge for the six kilometres he never asked for.

The SGD 2.00 Adam Road gantry — the off-optimal-route line — is ALREADY comprehended in that refund under POL-RD-09(1), because the recomputed fare carries only the on-route Kim Keat Link gantry: the difference between the 4.50 actually billed and the 2.50 recomputed sits inside the 13.68. It is itemised for transparency and must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The 2.50 on-route gantry properly stands.

No escalation trigger fires on this record. The trace is clean, the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and the driver's congestion assertion cites no artifact at all — POL-RD-08 says a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. That is an undischarged defence, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, which requires an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool. The record is sufficient to move money and the case should be ruled, not held.

The rider's own profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, not 4 or more, so no independent source beyond the trace is required for this claim. I cite only that field, for the test that names it.

The established deviation is not additionally MATERIAL: 5.97 km is 33.17%, below the 50% test, and below the 8.0 km absolute test. No POL-RD-06 driver-profile pattern finding is sought and none is needed — the rider's remedy rests entirely on this trip's own trace and the fare arithmetic, and no adverse finding is built on either party's reputation.

claims.text: On this trip's own trace a route deviation is established, and I do not contest it: the governing GPS polyline measures 23.97 km against the 18.0 km booked optimal, an excess of 5.97 km or 33.17%, which clears both POL-RD-01 gates (20% and 0.8 km). What the same figures do not do is reach MATERIALITY — that requires an excess above 50% of optimal (9.0 km) or above 8.0 km absolute, and 5.97 km fails both. This is an ordinary, not a material, deviation, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile consultation and its FULL_REFUND uplift are not engaged on this trip.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be built here, on the only figures POL-RD-06 permits. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 412 — a ratio of 0.24%, far below the 0.05 ratio the clause requires, and a raw flag count far below the 3 it also requires. The uplift to FULL_REFUND and the conduct referral therefore both fall away. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is a different quantity and is context only; POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it for the trailing-90-day figure.

The 1.6 surge is properly chargeable and belongs to no refund. fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.6 and, on this rate card, applies to base, distance and time only — never to the 4.50 of ERP — and POL-RD-02 requires the multiplier to be read from the fare_breakdown and carried into any recomputed fare. The 19.80 surge line therefore stands whatever else is decided, and no part of it is recoverable by the rider.

The 2.00 Adam Road gantry lies off the optimal route, but under POL-RD-09(1) that charge is already comprehended in any POL-RD-02 recomputation — which credits only gantries lying on the optimal route — and it must never be itemised as a separate correction and then added on top of the refund as a second recovery. By contrast the 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry does lie on the optimal route and is properly chargeable; the trip record confirms the optimal route crosses that gantry and nothing else.

There is no phantom-gantry billing-integrity correction available under POL-RD-09(4). The unbroken 100%-coverage trace passes within 250 m of both billed gantries — 0.0 m from the Kim Keat Link gantry and 8.76 m from the Adam Road gantry — so both lines are matched crossings of gantries the vehicle actually drove through, and neither may be refunded as an unmatched line.

The only explanation the driver offers for leaving the optimal corridor — that the AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit — is a traffic ground under POL-RD-03, and the artifact that clause requires is absent from the pool: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, and no LTA advisory covers the AYE, PIE or Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. An exculpatory ground asserted against an artifact missing from the pool is a POL-RD-10(5) trigger, and with the advisory absent the record cannot test the driver's explanation either way. The disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 rather than resolved against the driver on an empty record. Disclosure under POL-GEN-02: the advisory artifact relied on here is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is a route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-00114 (Bugis Junction to Jurong East, 7 Aug 2026). The rider's claim succeeds in part; the driver's explanation of the detour is not supported by the record.

THE DEVIATION. gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs (POL-RD-01). The trace (EV-GPS-00114, weight 1.0; 241 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps) measures 23.97 km against the 18.0 km booked optimal on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00114, weight 1.0). The excess is 5.97 km, or 33.17%, clearing both POL-RD-01 gates (20% and 0.8 km): the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06's driver-profile consultation, its FULL_REFUND uplift and its conduct referral are not engaged; on the citable figures there is no repeat pattern in any event (deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 412 completed trips in 90 days). The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used; the claim mentioning it did so only to exclude it, so nothing is discarded on that account.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC GROUND. You say the AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit and that you went up and over on the PIE, and you accept you know of no advisory. POL-RD-03 exonerates a deviation only where a traffic advisory names the affected segment, has a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows you reaching it, and the actual route leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor. No such advisory exists: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload). Your point is therefore a general assertion of bad traffic with no artifact behind it; under POL-RD-08 it does not discharge your burden here. It is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation: that trigger requires an exculpatory clause invoked in reliance on a cited artifact that is missing, and none was relied on — the absent advisory carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)); only its absence is citable. I therefore rule on the record rather than holding it. POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) and POL-RD-05 (endpoint amendment) do not apply either: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00114) records no rider instruction and waypoint_hint is null, and no endpoint was amended.

THE FARE RECOMPUTATION (POL-RD-02; fare_model METERED). The multiplier 1.6 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-00114) and is carried into the recomputed fare; it does not touch the 4.50 of ERP.
- charged_total: SGD 58.10
- recomputed_fare: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 optimal-route ERP = SGD 44.42
- refund: 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to SGD 13.70

The off-route Adam Road gantry charge of 2.00 is ALREADY comprehended in that refund (the recomputation credits only the on-route Kim Keat Link gantry of 2.50) and is itemised for transparency only; it must never be added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). Both gantries are matched crossings — the trace passes within 250 m of each (0.0 m and 8.76 m) — so there is no phantom line and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral. The outcome for this rider-filed dispute is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70.

The trace is clean: 241 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so POL-RD-07 does not impair it and no independent corroboration is required. The rider's identity showing (same trip_id TRP-00114 across the three platform artifacts) is accepted. Because the excess is 33.2% and 5.97 km, below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality lines, POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises — the profile check would in any event find no pattern (1 deviation flag in 412 completed trips in 90 days). DRIVER: your explanation that the AYE was crawling so you went up and over on the PIE does not change the outcome. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic advisory naming the affected road or segment for the trip window; there is none, and you told us you knew of none. Under POL-RD-08, once the rider has shown a threshold excess the burden shifts to you to point to a specific artifact and clause, and a general assertion that traffic was bad does not discharge that burden — so the deviation stands against you. This is not a case that must be held for a human reviewer: you cited no advisory, so there is no missing artifact to look up, and a bare assertion is resolved against the party who must prove it rather than escalated. On the money: the 1.6 surge is read from the fare breakdown, applies to base, distance and time only and never to ERP, and is not contested — it stands. The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02: ((3.80 + 0.75 × 18.0 + 0.28 × 30) × 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-route ERP = 44.42 recomputed, against a charged total of 58.10, giving 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70. The 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route but is already comprehended in that figure under POL-RD-09(1) — the recomputation credits only the on-route Kim Keat Link gantry — and is not added on top; the trace passes within 250 m of both gantries, so neither is a phantom line and there is no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) for them. The Adam Road charge is itemised here only for transparency. The traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00114-01 carries weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact and this ruling fixes no finding on it — what is used is permitted: the absence itself as a citation. The deciding facts (the measured excess and the fare arithmetic) rest on the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown, all at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. Result: the deviation is established but not material, no exculpatory clause runs, and SGD 13.70 of the SGD 58.10 charged is refunded to the rider; the remaining charge stands.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this is the fare on trip TRP-00114 (Bugis Junction to Jurong East, Friday 7 August 2026), charged at SGD 58.10. The rider accepts the 1.6 surge and disputes only the extra distance. Both advocates agree on the core facts, and so do I.

Route deviation. All three platform artifacts carry trip_id TRP-00114 and the trace's first fix (18:40) matches the recorded start, so the trip is identified and the rider's limb (a) under POL-RD-08 is met. On distance the GPS polyline governs: EV-GPS-00114 records 23.97 km, and that is the figure I use, not the rounded 24.0 km on the trip record. Against the booked optimal of 18.0 km (EV-TRIP-00114) the excess is 5.97 km, or 33.17%. That clears both POL-RD-01 gates (above 20% and above 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED and limb (b) is met. It does not reach materiality (which needs more than 50% or more than 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 driver-profile review, FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral arises.

Trace integrity. 241 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, with no 500 m jumps. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

Exoneration. Nothing excuses the deviation. No endpoint was amended (the POL-RD-05 fields are null). The chat log shows the rider challenging the route and the driver answering that he chose the corridor; there is no rider instruction and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. The driver's explanation — that the AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit — is a traffic ground, and to exonerate under POL-RD-03 it needs a traffic advisory naming the affected segment with an overlapping validity window. EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and no LTA advisory covers the AYE, PIE or Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. Under POL-GEN-02 that absence is citable but carries no fact and does not cap my confidence, because the facts that decide this case sit on the clean, weight-1.0 artifacts. I have considered whether the absent advisory should send the case to a human reviewer. It should not: POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden, and POL-RD-10(5) has nothing to bite on because the driver named no advisory to be missing. The record is complete and sufficient to rule.

Fare arithmetic (metered, so POL-RD-02 applies):
- charged_total: SGD 58.10
- recomputed_fare: (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6 + 0.80 + 2.50 = 25.70 x 1.6 + 3.30 = 41.12 + 3.30 = SGD 44.42
- refund: 58.10 - 44.42 = SGD 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70.
The surge multiplier of 1.6 is read from EV-FARE-00114 and the rider accepts it. The recomputed fare credits only the ERP on the optimal route, the Kim Keat Link gantry at 2.50. The Adam Road gantry at 2.00 is off the optimal route and is already comprehended in the refund under POL-RD-09(1); it is not added on top. Both billed gantries sit within 250 m of trace fixes (0.0 m and 8.8 m), so neither is a phantom line and there is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding.

No driver compensation is due: the distance billed (24.0 km) is not less than the trace records, so the POL-RD-04 compensation limb does not arise. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below 90% of the total, so this is a partial, not a full, refund.

Outcome: SGD 13.70 is returned to the rider; the remainder of the fare stands.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — ruling on trip TRP-00114 (Bugis Junction to Jurong East MRT, Friday 7 August 2026).

DEVIATION. The governing distance is the GPS trace, not the trip record's rounded copy: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km (23.97 km) govern over the 24.0 km convenience figure, against a booked optimal of 18.0 km. The excess is 5.97 km, or 33.2% of optimal, clearing both the 0.8 km and 20% establishment gates, so the deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (241 fixes, 10-second spacing, 100% coverage, zero gaps), so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The excess does NOT reach MATERIALITY (which needs above 50% or above 8.0 km), so no driver-profile pattern finding arises and no conduct referral follows. The driver's own trailing-90-day figures (deviation_flags_90d 1 over 412 completed trips) would not establish a pattern in any event; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used.

FARE. The trip is METERED, so the remedy is the arithmetic of POL-RD-02, carrying the 1.6 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier — which the rider accepts.
  • Charged_total: 58.10
  • Recomputed_fare: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-route ERP = (25.70 x 1.6) + 3.30 = 44.42
  • Refund: 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70
The 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route but is already comprehended in that 13.70 — the recomputed fare credits only the on-route Kim Keat Link gantry — so it is itemised for transparency and is NOT added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). Both billed gantries are matched crossings (the trace passes within 250 m of each), so no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) is available. The refund is above the 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of the charge, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

EXCULPATION. POL-RD-03 cannot run: it requires an LTA traffic advisory naming an affected segment, and the only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; the driver's own statement concedes he knows of no advisory. POL-RD-04 cannot run: the chat log shows the rider questioning the route ('adam road?? jurong is the other way'), not requesting a detour, and waypoint_hint is null. POL-RD-05 cannot run: neither endpoint was amended.

ESCALATION DECLINED. I do not hold the case. The driver's ground — 'AYE jam' — is an assertion citing no evidence ID and no advisory. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged because the driver invokes no artifact that could be missing: this is an undischarged defence, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact absent from the pool. The record is complete, the trace is clean and the arithmetic is exact, so the case is decided rather than escalated.

The rider's profile (1 deviation claim in 60 days) does not engage the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay, and no clause in this category produces a referral.

OUTCOME. The rider's claim is partly upheld: SGD 13.70 is refunded to the rider; the balance of the contested SGD 15.00 is not, and the 1.6 surge the rider accepted stands.

The rider has therefore carried limb (a) of the initial burden — the artifacts are of this trip and no identity objection is open.

The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record: under POL-RD-01 gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two disagree, so the actual distance is 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — a measured excess of 5.97 km. The trip record's 24.0 km may not be cited for the threshold test.

Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass on those figures: the excess is 33.17% of the 18.0 km optimal route, above the 20% test, and 5.97 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km test. The route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace and limb (b) of POL-RD-08 is satisfied.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 241 fixes at a 10 second sample interval across 100% coverage, no gaps at all and max_gap_sec of 0.0, and no consecutive-fix jump anywhere near the 500 m limb. The only exculpatory route open to the driver is POL-RD-03, and it cannot run. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic_advisory naming an affected segment with an overlapping validity window; its absence is itself citable and it exonerates nothing. The driver's own statement concedes he knows of no advisory.

POL-RD-04 does not apply either. The two-message chat log shows the rider challenging the route — 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' at 18:58:40 — and the driver answering 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' at 18:59:20, which is an admission that the driver chose the corridor. There is no rider instruction, no named road requested by the rider, and waypoint_hint is null, so the rider-requested-detour clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

Nor was either endpoint amended: amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null and no pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at is recorded, so POL-RD-05 has no amended re-quote to re-price the trip against and cannot excuse any part of the 5.97 km excess.

That is comfortably above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome for this rider-filed dispute is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70, leaving the rider not carrying the charge for the six kilometres he never asked for.

The SGD 2.00 Adam Road gantry — the off-optimal-route line — is ALREADY comprehended in that refund under POL-RD-09(1), because the recomputed fare carries only the on-route Kim Keat Link gantry: the difference between the 4.50 actually billed and the 2.50 recomputed sits inside the 13.68. It is itemised for transparency and must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The 2.50 on-route gantry properly stands.

ledger.claim: The 1.6 surge is properly chargeable and belongs to no refund. fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.6 and, on this rate card, applies to base, distance and time only — never to the 4.50 of ERP — and POL-RD-02 requires the multiplier to be read from the fare_breakdown and carried into any recomputed fare. The 19.80 surge line therefore stands whatever else is decided, and no part of it is recoverable by the rider.

The 2.00 Adam Road gantry lies off the optimal route, but under POL-RD-09(1) that charge is already comprehended in any POL-RD-02 recomputation — which credits only gantries lying on the optimal route — and it must never be itemised as a separate correction and then added on top of the refund as a second recovery. By contrast the 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry does lie on the optimal route and is properly chargeable; the trip record confirms the optimal route crosses that gantry and nothing else.

There is no phantom-gantry billing-integrity correction available under POL-RD-09(4). The unbroken 100%-coverage trace passes within 250 m of both billed gantries — 0.0 m from the Kim Keat Link gantry and 8.76 m from the Adam Road gantry — so both lines are matched crossings of gantries the vehicle actually drove through, and neither may be refunded as an unmatched line.

The only explanation the driver offers for leaving the optimal corridor — that the AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit — is a traffic ground under POL-RD-03, and the artifact that clause requires is absent from the pool: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, and no LTA advisory covers the AYE, PIE or Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. An exculpatory ground asserted against an artifact missing from the pool is a POL-RD-10(5) trigger, and with the advisory absent the record cannot test the driver's explanation either way. The disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 rather than resolved against the driver on an empty record. Disclosure under POL-GEN-02: the advisory artifact relied on here is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT.
